page: Microsoft Azure D32alds_v7 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the Daldsv7 family. It features 32 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low-memory allocation of 2.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled, providing 1890 GB of local disk capacity with Premium Storage capability. The virtualization is managed via Microsoft Hyper-V.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier single-core performance. The stress-ng single-core CPU test and single-threaded gzip compression both rank in the top 10% tier. Multi-threaded performance is also competitive, with the passmark CPU score and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression ranking in the top 25% tier. However, multi-core stress-ng CPU performance and database operations fall into the average tier, reflecting the constraints of the 2.0 GB per core memory allocation on highly parallel, memory-intensive tasks.

This server offers high compute density and fast clock speeds, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for compute-bound workloads that do not require large memory footprints. The 1890 GB of local storage provides high-speed local scratch space, though the low memory-to-vCPU ratio represents a tradeoff for memory-heavy databases. Appropriate workloads include single-threaded processing tasks, web serving, and lightweight machine learning inference, as demonstrated by its top-tier text generation speed on small models.
description: Microsoft Azure D32alds_v7 is an x86_64 compute-optimized server from the Daldsv7 family, powered by a 32-vCPU AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz. It features a dedicated CPU allocation across 16 physical cores, paired with 64.0 GB of memory and 1890 GB of local storage. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, this server exhibits top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core and single-threaded gzip compression benchmarks placing in the top 10%. While multi-core processing and memory bandwidth sit in the average tier, the instance delivers strong performance in static web serving and small-model LLM text generation. The low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core makes it a qualitatively cost-efficient choice for compute-heavy, memory-light workloads such as web serving, file compression, and lightweight inference tasks.
